findings.title: Automatic review overwrites a pharmacist hold
findings.reproduce: Start scanFill for Rx 0072214 with review=none and pause the model response. While paused, submit a valid pharmacist change request; confirm review=on_hold. Release the model. The review becomes clear and the scan fills the order.
findings.impact: A pharmacist decision made during an automatic review is lost, and an order awaiting a prescriber change can proceed to filling.
findings.fix: Persist automatic findings using a conditional update against the current order version and review state. Revalidate review and version inside the fill transaction. Do not rely on the review value read before an await.
findings.accept: The hold and change-request record survive model completion; the scan returns a conflict and creates no dispense. Repeat with reject, approve, order edits and simultaneous review runs.

screenshots.caption: The awaited review writes using the old review state. The test first verifies that a valid pharmacist request put the order on hold.
Prescription review workflow. Earlier synthetic browser rehearsal; workflow context only, not a capture of the backend failure.

findings.title: Pending destination recall prevents confirmation from propagating
findings.basis: Two-store acceptance reproduction and successful fresh-destination control
findings.reproduce: Store 2 looks up D-0611-2026 without confirmation. Store 7 then looks up and confirms it. Store 2 retains confirmed_at=null because INSERT OR IGNORE preserves its existing pending row.
findings.impact: The other store can continue to hold affected packages on the shelf despite confirmation at Store 7. The current test covers only a destination without the pending row.
findings.fix: Merge confirmation into an existing pending recall-lot row, with provenance and audit, before quarantining. Treat propagation as idempotent and retryable.
findings.accept: Both a fresh destination and a destination with a pending row end with GX4471C confirmed, zero on-shelf affected packages, and receiving/fill/register/transfer blocks. Repeat confirmation and restart must not duplicate work.

screenshots.caption: INSERT OR IGNORE does not upgrade an existing pending row. A fresh destination passes the same acceptance control.
Recall workflow. Earlier synthetic browser rehearsal; workflow context only, not a capture of the backend failure.

findings.title: Clinical reads bypass cashier and admin role restrictions
findings.basis: HTTP reproduction plus ten failed role acceptance checks
findings.reproduce: After a pharmacist runs Guardian and confirms a recall, sign in as cashier m.diaz or admin s.grant. GET /api/agents/runs, /api/agents/rx-guardian, /api/recalls, /api/recalls/D-0611-2026 and /api/recalls/D-0611-2026/results. Each returns 200. Agent output contains patient IDs with clinical history; recall output exposes patient-linked impact or outreach information. /api/suggestions correctly returns 403.
findings.impact: Hiding clinical screens and protecting the patient endpoint does not protect alternate reads of the same data.
findings.fix: Define an explicit read authorization matrix. Gate clinical run history and recall patient details; return a separate minimal summary where a role needs counts. Filter by agent and role before serialization.
findings.accept: Anonymous reads return 401. Cashier/admin clinical detail reads return 403, or an explicitly specified sanitized summary without patient-linked clinical data. Pharmacist and permitted technician reads still work. Cover all downloads, audio, search, nested results and partner scopes.

screenshots.caption: The read path has no explicit role check. The same cashier is correctly blocked from /api/suggestions.
AI agents workflow. Earlier synthetic browser rehearsal; workflow context only, not a capture of the backend failure.

findings.title: Current locally sold medicines are omitted from some safety rules
findings.basis: Pure-rule comparison with a passing Active control
findings.reproduce: Evaluate a ciprofloxacin order with a two-day-old 68-day insulin fill. With history.status=Active the Guardian emits its fluoroquinolone/insulin demo-table interaction. Change only status to Sold here, the status loadHistory assigns to local dispenses: no hit is emitted.
findings.impact: A new local sale can be present in history but absent from interaction or duplicate-therapy evaluation. This finding demonstrates software inconsistency, not clinical accuracy of the synthetic rule.
findings.fix: Unify active-medication derivation across imported history, local dispenses, Watcher and Guardian using supply dates and discontinuation state. Avoid merely changing every historical sale to Active.
findings.accept: Receive/fill/verify/sell an unseeded current medicine, create the next relevant order and verify the expected demo rule. Include expired supply, discontinued medicine, duplicate imported/local history and corrected orders.

screenshots.caption: History added from local sales uses Sold here. This filter accepts only Active; the otherwise identical Active control passes.

findings.title: Interrupted cross-store transfer duplicates available stock
findings.basis: Injected source-write failure after destination commit
findings.reproduce: Select an on-shelf AMX0626C package. Inject a source database trigger that aborts its transfer-out update. Transfer one unit to Store 2. The operation throws, but the destination has already committed. The serial remains on_shelf in both stores.
findings.impact: The same physical serial is offered as available twice. A user retry does not provide an explicit reconciliation or durable transfer state.
findings.fix: Use a durable transfer ID and state machine with a source reservation, idempotent destination receipt, commit acknowledgement and recovery/reconciliation. A local transaction around one database does not make two files atomic.
findings.accept: Inject failure before and after each write boundary, restart and retry. At most one store can offer the serial. Incomplete transfers remain visible and recoverable, with consistent audit records.

screenshots.caption: Destination and source commit separately. The injected source write failure leaves both copies on_shelf.
Transfer workflow. Earlier synthetic browser rehearsal; workflow context only, not a capture of the backend failure.

findings.title: Store 2 outputs retain Store 7 identity and contact details
findings.reproduce: Use Store 2 to draft default recall outreach or generate its recall PDF. Templates hardcode Elm Street, J. Rivera and Store 7 phone; the PDF heading hardcodes Store 7. Store 2 has a different name, pharmacist and phone.
findings.impact: A correctly scoped patient list can still produce a misattributed report or direct a recipient to the wrong pharmacy.
findings.fix: Resolve pharmacy name, phone and signing actor from the current store at draft, preview, send and export time. Review voice templates and AI draft merging too.
findings.accept: Store 2 previews, sandbox sends and PDF use Birch Avenue, its own contact details and the approving actor. Store 7 remains correct. Do not count the fixed manufacturer-response path as coverage for all outputs.

screenshots.caption: Store 2 identity and phone are correct in /api/me. The draft response still contains Elm Street and Store 7 phone.

findings.title: Provider destination policy accepts mapped link-local addresses
findings.basis: Provider-settings API accepted the URL; no metadata request made
findings.reproduce: As an authorized pharmacist/admin, set baseUrl to http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest. The API returns 200 although literal 169.254 addresses are rejected. The settings were restored after this test.
findings.impact: The intended metadata-destination block is incomplete. Exploitation depends on configuration privileges, connectivity and the adapter POST path. Credential theft was not demonstrated.
findings.fix: Normalize and validate IP families and resolved destinations, including redirects. Make permitted local-model endpoints explicit. Bind stored credentials to approved origins when endpoints change.
findings.accept: IPv4, IPv6 mapped addresses, hostname resolution and redirect cases follow the same destination policy. Rejected destinations receive no request or credential. Intended localhost model endpoints remain usable.

screenshots.caption: The policy checks a literal IPv4 prefix; a mapped IPv6 hostname passes. No request was sent to the metadata service.

findings.title: Windows file-key permissions do not meet the owner-only claim
findings.basis: Three Windows permission test failures and inspected generated-key ACL
findings.reproduce: Run the file-key provider on this Windows host. POSIX mode assertions report 0666 rather than 0600. The generated key also inherits a read grant to the local CodexSandboxUsers group in addition to the owner, SYSTEM and Administrators.
findings.impact: chmod does not establish the claimed owner-only boundary on this platform. This is not evidence of public access.
findings.fix: Define supported deployment platforms and enforce an appropriate Windows DACL, or require externally supplied keys on Windows. Document and test the actual access boundary.
findings.accept: An unauthorized local account cannot read the current, retired or temporary key files. Tests validate Windows ACLs on Windows and POSIX modes on Linux. Key rotation and restore still work.

screenshots.caption: POSIX chmod is not a Windows DACL. The inspected key inherits a read grant; no key material is displayed.
